assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made artificial atoms coherently measurable and controllable through microwave photons, opening a durable experimental regime of quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: The proposed laureates represent decisive theoretical, experimental and architectural contributions, although the credited four-person framing leaves difficult choices.
assessment.maturity: The methods are reproduced widely and underpin a major mature experimental field.
uncertainties: Whether this advance is judged sufficiently distinct from already rewarded superconducting-circuit breakthroughs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction supplied the central physical principle showing how reliable quantum information can emerge from faulty quantum components.
assessment.attribution: Shor, Steane and Kitaev made individually identifiable foundational contributions to codes and fault tolerance.
assessment.maturity: The theory is long established and experimental demonstrations increasingly test its essential claims.
uncertainties: Large-scale fault-tolerant computation has not yet been achieved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped ions provided one of the clearest routes from quantum-control principles to programmable many-body quantum systems and computation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supplied seminal concepts, while Blatt led decisive experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: Ion-trap control has been replicated and developed over decades into an exceptionally precise platform.
uncertainties: The conceptual overlap with broader trapped-ion and optical-lattice nominations requires careful delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks transformed precision timekeeping by combining extreme atomic-clock accuracy with control of motion-induced shifts.
assessment.attribution: Katori and Ye are clear central figures in the invention and realization of the platform.
assessment.maturity: Independent laboratories have demonstrated remarkable precision and broad scientific utility.
uncertainties: The eventual practical definition of the second depends on continuing international metrology decisions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric and topological phases revealed that quantum phase has observable physical content beyond local classical fields and energies.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Berry are the unmistakable names attached to the two central effects in the proposed framing.
assessment.maturity: Both effects are longstanding, repeatedly observed, and foundational across quantum and condensed-matter physics.
uncertainties: The two effects arose in different contexts, so the unity of the citation would need a persuasive formulation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum optomechanics made collective mechanical motion accessible to preparation, measurement and coherent quantum control.
assessment.attribution: The proposed names cover major experimental and conceptual routes into cavity optomechanics and quantum acoustics.
assessment.maturity: The core effects have been robustly reproduced, including ground-state and quantum-regime experiments.
uncertainties: Attribution across optical, microwave and acoustic implementations is broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological-insulator framework established a new class of quantum matter with robust boundary physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the defining theory, while Molenkamp represents crucial experimental establishment.
assessment.maturity: The phase and its characteristic boundary phenomena are now established across materials and experiments.
uncertainties: There is substantial overlap with other topological-insulator and quantum-anomalous-Hall nominations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned coherent matter waves into exceptionally powerful probes of gravity, inertial motion and fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: The three proposed laureates made major distinct contributions to the conceptual and precision-measurement foundations.
assessment.maturity: The techniques are established across many laboratories and applications.
uncertainties: The field has many foundational contributors, making a three-person attribution difficult.
